case_title: Charandas Swami v. State of Gujarat & Anr.
accused_occupation: Temple functionaries: Accused 1 was Assistant Kothari; Accused 2 informally assisted him; Accused 3-5 were henchmen of Accused 1 and 2
accused_socioeconomic_status: Accused 1 and 2 had large unexplained cash and investments found at their residence; no other class or wealth finding stated
accused_victim_relationship: Administrative/political rivals: the victim, as newly elected Board Chairman, proposed transferring Accused 1 and associates, who feared exposure of their misdeeds
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.120-B; s.364 (r/w s.120-B); s.201 (r/w s.120-B) for Accused 2 and 5
weapon: Not stated (death by strangulation; a cloth 'khesiya' appears only in the account given in Accused 3's panchnama)
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence (last seen, motive, recovery of body, disclosures, medical identification, conduct, call records); some hostile eyewitnesses
confession: No confession as such; disclosures by Accused 3 and Accused 5 leading to discovery of the dump site and crime room were admitted under s.27 and relied on
aggravating_circumstances: Body burnt and dumped in a ditch in another State; vehicle burnt; false insurance claim filed; attempts to mislead investigation
trial_court_outcome: Convicted all five accused under s.302 r/w s.120-B (death sentence); s.364 r/w s.120-B (life rigorous imprisonment); Accused 2 and 5 also s.201 r/w s.120-B (5 years RI)
high_court_outcome: Conviction of Accused 1, 2, 3, 5 confirmed; Accused 4 acquitted; death sentence commuted to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Murder (s.302 r/w s.120-B); kidnapping (s.364 r/w s.120-B) for Accused 1, 2, 5; s.201 r/w s.120-B for Accused 2 and 5
neutral_facts: The victim, the newly elected chairman of a temple trust board, had proposed transferring a senior temple official and his associates, who feared exposure of financial irregularities. The victim was last seen on a afternoon in a blue car with one of the accused, leaving the temple premises. Witnesses who initially said they saw the victim leave the temple later turned hostile, though the court weighed their admissible parts together with other testimony. According to the prosecution, the accused took the victim to another temple complex, where a call girl was procured through a co-accused, the victim was sedated and then strangled. Cellular records showed a co-accused in contact with the person who brought the woman. A burnt, unidentified body was later found in a ditch in a neighbouring State the next day. Following a disclosure by one of the accused, the body was identified through a key tied with cotton thread matching the victim's room lock, gold dental caps, and DNA comparison with a blood sample from the victim's sister. A post-mortem recorded death by asphyxia from strangulation and homicide. The car used was later found burnt in a garage, and an insurance claim for it was rejected after a surveyor found no accidental or mechanical cause for the burning. A disclosure by another accused led police to the crime location, where a panchnama recorded the discovery of the room and of tablets.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to strangulation; body subsequently burnt and dumped in a ditch
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.302, 120-B, 364, 201); 4 finally upheld across appellants (s.201 for Accused 2 and 5 only; s.302, 120-B, 364 for Accused 1 and 5)
financial_property_loss: Alleged misappropriation of temple funds and kickbacks; amounts not quantified in the judgment
premeditation_planning: Yes: Supreme Court accepted a conspiracy hatched and executed; trial court also found the crime involved pre-planning
motive: Accused 1 and 2 feared transfer from the temple and loss of control over affairs, exposure of their financial irregularities
key_evidence_accepted: Last-seen evidence; recovery of body and DNA/dental/key identification; s.27 disclosures by Accused 3 and 5; call records and call-girl identification; burning of car and false insurance claim
witness_credibility: Hostile witnesses (PW14, PW15, PW25, PW42, PW43, PW49) partly relied on for admissible parts; PW30 credible for panchnama; PW32 independent and accepted; discrepancies in medical records held not to discredit identity
post_offence_conduct: Body dumped and burnt in another State; car burnt; false accident insurance claim filed under Accused 3's signature; misled investigating agencies
bail_history: Accused were on bail at the Supreme Court stage; ordered to surrender forthwith. Other bail history not stated
trial_duration: offence: 03.05.1998; trial judgment: 11.06.2004; High Court: 01.09.2006; Supreme Court: 10.04.2017
legal_representation: Appellants: Huzefa Ahmadi and K.T.S. Tulsi, Sr. Advs. (with others); Respondent/State: Ms. Kiran Suri, Sr. Adv. (with others)
investigation_status: Missing complaint filed; investigation transferred to CBI; CBI FIR 29.10.1998; all five accused arrested; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Investigating authorities lacked care in choosing panchas with prior disputes with accused (held not to make evidence inadmissible); some FIR-named persons dropped from chargesheet
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted all five, death sentence. High Court: conviction of 1, 2, 3, 5 upheld, Accused 4 acquitted, death commuted to life. Supreme Court: appeals of Accused 1, 2, 5 dismissed; Accused 3 did not appeal
prosecution_argument: Conspiracy may be proved by inference; guilt established through motive, last-seen theory, place of murder, disposal of body, panchnama and recovery of body, conduct of Accused 3, and financial irregularities
defence_argument: No evidence of meeting of minds; motive imaginary; last-seen theory falls flat; panchnama under s.27 inadmissible; medical and DNA evidence unreliable; other persons inimical to the victim
legal_principle_applied: Concurrent findings not disturbed unless perverse; conspiracy may be proved by inference from proved circumstances; s.27 admissibility of disclosure limited to distinctly discovered facts
precedent_relied_upon: Subbaiah Ambalam v State of Tamil Nadu AIR 1977 SC 2046; State of Karnataka v David Rozario (2002) 7 SCC 728; Baliya alias Bal Kishan v State of MP (2012) 9 SCC 696; Pulukuri Kottaya v Emperor AIR 1947 PC 67; Mohmed Inayatullah v State of Maharashtra (1976) 1 SCC 828; State (NCT of Delhi) v Navjot Sandhu (2005) 11 SCC 600; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (Supreme Court upheld the High Court's life sentence without separate sentencing reasoning)
judicial_aggravating_factors: None weighed by the Supreme Court; trial court called offence heinous (prosecution and High Court did not support rarest-of-rare classification)
other_sentence_order: Accused on bail directed to surrender forthwith
